chunks: And with this chain of narrators, it was said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

Shall I not inform you why the believer is called a believer? It is because of the trustworthiness of people in entrusting him with their souls and wealth. Shall I not inform you about the Muslim? The Muslim is the one from whose hand and tongue people are safe. Shall I not inform you about the Muhajir (emigrant)? He is the one who desists from sins and leaves behind the evil deeds and what Allah has forbidden.
ai.seo_question: What are the defining characteristics of a true Muslim and believer according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Sifat al-Shia* delineates the tripartite identity of the faithful, linking external social trust (Iman) with internal moral purity (Islam) and spiritual migration (Hijra). It reflects the Shia emphasis on the integration of social reliability and ethical conduct as defining marks of true faith, where 'emigration' is interpreted not merely as physical movement but as a continuous departure from sin.

en.badr-shahin: (The same series of relaters)… The Prophet (s) said:

Do you know why the believers are called so? This is because people can entrust them with their souls and fortunes. May I tell you about the true Muslims? The true Muslims are those from whose hands –i.e. acts- and tongues –i.e. words- people are saved. May I tell you about the true Muhajirs? They are those who deserted the sins as well as everything that Allah has forbidden.
